possibly_relevant_provisions.title: Identity theft
possibly_relevant_provisions.relevance: Fraudulent use of another person's unique identification feature (e.g. impersonation using their likeness/account).

possibly_relevant_provisions.title: Violation of privacy
possibly_relevant_provisions.relevance: Capturing, publishing or transmitting images of a person's private area without consent.

possibly_relevant_provisions.title: Publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form
Publishing or transmitting material containing sexually explicit acts
Offences such as voyeurism, stalking, insulting the modesty of a woman, extortion, cheating by personation, criminal intimidation, forgery and defamation
possibly_relevant_provisions.relevance: The police decide which BNS sections apply to the facts. Section numbers changed from the IPC, so confirm current numbers with the police or a lawyer.

possibly_relevant_provisions.law: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
possibly_relevant_provisions.title: Removal of intimate or impersonating (including artificially morphed) content on the depicted person's complaint
possibly_relevant_provisions.relevance: Intermediaries are required to remove such content within 2 hours of a complaint by (or on behalf of) the depicted person about content that shows them in intimate or sexual content, or impersonates them, including artificially morphed images (shortened from 24 hours by the 2026 amendment, G.S.R. 120(E), in force 20 Feb 2026). Confirm the current rule text.

possibly_relevant_provisions.title: Platform grievance redressal (acknowledge and resolve complaints within set timelines)
Appeal against a platform grievance officer's decision

possibly_relevant_provisions.law: IT Rules amendments on synthetically generated information
